summary: Follow-up plan for stage GN.3 (Reduction, mass and theta series) of the geometry-of-numbers roadmap, citing the sixteen GN.3 nodes of the accepted base packet. It plans reduction domains (Minkowski-reduced bases of real lattices and their Siegel-set containment over AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3; minus continued fractions, reduction cycles and Pell automorphs of indefinite binary forms beyond IntegralLattices B2–B5); finite-field counts (Gaussian binomials, finite orthogonal group orders, isometry and isotropic-subspace counts in the orthogonal, unitary and symplectic cases); quadratic local representation densities with stabilization, Hanke's reduction maps and closed forms, uniform bounds, the orthogonal Cho–Yamauchi formula, Li–Zhang's Siegel series with Ikeda's functional equations, the induction formula (with a corrected corollary), horizontal lattices and Siegel's main theorem; hermitian densities beyond the base packet: the representation scheme, stabilization, primitive and saturation steps, cancellation, central derivative, special values, Terstiege's induction, almost self-dual targets, the split case, Hironaka's analytic proof of the functional equation, the ramified densities of Li–Liu and He–Li–Shi–Yang's primitive derivative formula; mass: trace lattices over totally real fields, proper/ordinary doubling, Kirschmer's local types and factors with Gan–Hanke–Yu's smooth models and canonical volumes, archimedean constants, Euler products at integers ≥ 2 (no continuation of ζ_K needed), Weil's operators and Siegel formula for m > 4, τ(SO_Q) = 2, the unitary mass formula with Lipnowski–Tsimerman's asymptotics and local orbit counts; and theta series of definite lattices with genus averages and the Hecke Eisenstein average over totally real fields.

nodes.title: Minkowski-reduced bases of a Euclidean lattice
nodes.statement: Let E be a real inner-product space of finite dimension n and L ⊂ E a discrete full Z-submodule. An ordered Z-basis (b_1,…,b_n) of L is Minkowski-reduced when, for each i = 1,…,n, b_i has the least length ‖b_i‖ among all v ∈ L such that (b_1,…,b_{i−1},v) extends to a Z-basis of L. Equivalently, for each i, ‖b_i‖ ≤ ‖v‖ for every v ∈ L whose coefficient vector in the basis has gcd(c_i,…,c_n) = 1. The predicate depends only on the Gram matrix (⟨b_i,b_j⟩), is preserved by changing the sign of any b_i, and is invariant under linear isometries of E.
hypotheses: E finite-dimensional real inner-product space, n = dim E (n = 0 allowed: the empty basis is reduced).
L discrete with IsZLattice ℝ L; bases are ordered and indexed by Fin n.
Lengths are Euclidean norms; no integrality of the Gram matrix is assumed.
proofSteps: Define the predicate through the extension condition, phrased with the primitive coefficient condition gcd(c_i,…,c_n) = 1 so that it is decidable from coefficients.

Existence: choose b_1 a shortest nonzero vector (finite-gauge-sublevel gives finitely many candidates under any bound), then inductively a shortest vector among those extending the partial basis; the set of candidates is nonempty because the partial basis extends (primitive completion in the free module L) and each candidate set under a bound is finite.
Sign and isometry invariance are immediate from the definition, which only uses lengths and the extension property.

For integral lattices over Z this is the predicate of IntegralLattices milestone 2G, which proves existence and the entry bounds for integral Gram matrices; this node is the real (non-integral) version that BSW use for the lattices attached to real binary forms.
acceptance: In Z² with the standard form, (e_1, e_2) is reduced and (e_1, e_1 + e_2) is not, since ‖e_2‖ < ‖e_1 + e_2‖ and e_2 extends e_1.
For the hexagonal lattice with basis b_1 = (1,0), b_2 = (1/2, √3/2), the basis is reduced and so are the bases obtained by sign changes.
Reduced bases need not realise the successive minima in dimension ≥ 5 (the vectors realising the minima need not form a basis), so the predicate is not 'attains every minimum'.

nodes.title: Reduced Gram matrices lie in a Siegel set
nodes.statement: For every n ≥ 1 there are constants C_n > 1 and t_n > 0 such that the Gram matrix B of any Minkowski-reduced basis of a lattice in ℝⁿ is (e, C_n)-reduced in the sense of AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3.2, and hence its determinant normalization det(B)^{-1/n}B lies in the image in SL_n(ℝ)/SO(n) of the standard Siegel set 𝔖_{t_n} of AA.3.2–3.3. The statement is a containment, not an equivalence: a point of the Siegel set need not be a reduced Gram matrix.
hypotheses: n ≥ 1; rank 0 is a point and is excluded from the normalization.
Gram matrices of arbitrary determinant are first normalized to determinant one (or the statement is made in GL_n^+(ℝ)/O(n)).
proofSteps: Write B = Uᵀ D U with U unipotent upper triangular and D diagonal (the Gram–Schmidt/Cholesky decomposition; Tau Ceti cholesky).

From reducedness, ‖b_i‖² ≤ ‖b_{i+1}‖² and the Minkowski inequality ∏‖b_i‖² ≤ c_n det B give d_i/d_{i+1} bounded below and |u_ij| bounded, with constants depending on n (the reduced-diagonal bound of IntegralLattices 2G in its real form).
These are exactly the (e, C)-reduced conditions of AA.3.2; AA.3.2 'Reduced forms and Siegel sets' gives the Siegel-set containment and the determinant-one version.
acceptance: In dimension 2 the reduced region is |2b₁₂| ≤ b₁₁ ≤ b₂₂, and its normalized image lies in the region Im τ ≥ √3/2 of the upper half-plane, a Siegel set.
diag(1, t) is reduced exactly when t ≥ 1; the matrices diag(1, t) with 0 < t < 1, normalized, leave every fixed Siegel set as t → 0, so the containment genuinely uses reducedness.
Rank 1: every positive 1×1 matrix is reduced and the normalized matrix is (1).

nodes.title: Minus continued fractions and reduced quadratic irrationals
nodes.statement: For an integer n_0 and integers n_1, n_2, … ≥ 2, the minus continued fraction ⟦n_0, n_1, n_2, …⟧ is the limit of n_0 − 1/(n_1 − 1/(n_2 − ⋯)). Every real irrational w has a unique such expansion, obtained by the digit n_0 = ⌊w⌋ + 1 and the remainder map w ↦ 1/(n_0 − w). A real quadratic irrational w with Galois conjugate w^σ is reduced when 0 < w^σ < 1 < w. For an eventually periodic expansion, its primitive cycle ((n_1,…,n_ℓ)) is the least period up to cyclic rotation; a cycle with all n_j = 2 does not occur for irrational w.
hypotheses: w real and irrational; for the cycle notions w is a real quadratic irrational.
The step uses the digit n_0 = ⌊w⌋ + 1, so that n_0 − w ∈ (0,1) and every subsequent digit is ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Define the digit map and the remainder map w ↦ 1/(⌊w⌋ + 1 − w) on irrationals.
Convergence: the convergents p_k/q_k satisfy p_k q_{k−1} − p_{k−1} q_k = −1 with increasing q_k, so the continued fraction converges and equals w; uniqueness follows from the digit constraints.
Eventual periodicity for quadratic irrationals follows by Lagrange's argument for this expansion: the remainders lie in a finite set of reduced irrationals of the same discriminant.
acceptance: √2 = ⟦2, 2, 4, 2, 4, …⟧: the remainders after the first digit are 1 + √2/2 and 2 + √2, both reduced, and the primitive cycle is ((2, 4)).
w = (3 + √5)/2 is reduced (its conjugate (3 − √5)/2 ≈ 0.382 lies in (0,1)), and its expansion is purely periodic with cycle ((3)): 1/(3 − w) = w.
No irrational w has a period consisting of 2's only: ⟦2, 2, 2, …⟧ = 1 is rational.

nodes.title: Reduction cycles of narrow ideal classes
nodes.statement: Let K be a real quadratic field of fundamental discriminant D > 0 with conjugation σ and narrow class group Cl⁺(K). (1) Every narrow class A contains ideals wZ + Z with w ∈ K, w > w^σ, and the minus continued fraction of each such w is eventually periodic with primitive cycle independent of the choice; the expansion is purely periodic iff w is reduced. (2) The cycle is a complete invariant of A, and its length ℓ_A equals the number of reduced w with wZ + Z ∈ A. (3) If w is reduced and represents A, then 1/w^σ represents A^{−1}, and its cycle is the reverse of that of w. (4) For a reduced primitive cycle (w_1,…,w_ℓ) representing A, ∏ w_j = ε_D, the least unit > 1 of norm 1 (equivalently the least totally positive unit > 1), each w_j < √D + 1, and ℓ_A > log ε_D / log(√D + 1).
hypotheses: D a positive fundamental discriminant; classes are narrow (strict) classes.
Cycles are counted with cyclic positions, not distinct values.
proofSteps: Use the form–ideal bijection of IntegralLattices B2 and the cycle finiteness of B5 for the class-group side.

Show that the remainder map preserves the class of wZ + Z and that reduced numbers are closed under it, with the reduced representatives forming one orbit (Zagier's reduction theory as summarized in DIT §2).
Reversal: the map w ↦ 1/w^σ sends reduced to reduced and reverses the digit sequence, using (2.2) of DIT.

The product of the remainders around a cycle is the unit by which the cycle's matrix acts on w; it is totally positive and generates the norm-one units, giving ε_D. The bounds w_j < √D + 1 give the length bound.
acceptance: For D = 5, the class number is 1 and the reduced numbers of the trivial class form one cycle whose product is ε_5 = (3 + √5)/2.
For D = 12 (K = Q(√3)) the narrow class group has order 2 and there are two cycles, exchanged by A ↦ JA (multiplication by the class of √3).
Without primitivity of the cycle (repeating a period twice) the product would be ε_D², so the cycle is taken primitive.

The bounds w < √D + 1 and ℓ_A > log ε_D / log(√D + 1).

nodes.title: Automorphs of indefinite binary forms and the fundamental unit
nodes.statement: Let Q = [a,b,c] be a primitive integral binary form of nonsquare discriminant d = b² − 4ac > 0, and (t,u) the solution of t² − du² = 4 with t,u ≥ 1 and u least. Then the proper automorph group of Q in PSL_2(Z) is infinite cyclic, generated by γ_Q = ±[[(t − bu)/2, −cu],[au, (t + bu)/2]]. The attracting fixed point of γ_Q is (−b + √d)/(2a). If Q comes from a narrow class of the fundamental discriminant D = d via Q(x,y) = N(x − wy)/N(𝔞), then ε_D = (t + u√D)/2 is the least totally positive unit > 1 (equivalently the least unit > 1 of norm 1), and γ_Q is the matrix of multiplication by ε_D in the basis (w,1).
hypotheses: d > 0 nonsquare; Q primitive (gcd(a,b,c) = 1), which holds automatically when d is fundamental.
proofSteps: Solve the automorph equation: g fixes Q iff g = [[(t − bu)/2, −cu],[au, (t + bu)/2]] with t² − du² = 4 (direct computation with the adjoint of the Gram matrix).

The solutions form a group isomorphic to the norm-one units of the order of discriminant d, which is infinite cyclic generated by (t + u√d)/2 for the least u (IntegralLattices B4 gives SO(L) ≅ norm-one units).

nodes.title: Gaussian binomial coefficients
nodes.statement: For an integer q and natural numbers n, k, the Gaussian binomial [n choose k]_q ∈ Z is ∏_{i=0}^{k−1} (q^{n−i} − 1)/(q^{i+1} − 1) when k ≤ n, interpreted through the recursion [n+1 choose k+1]_q = [n choose k]_q + q^{k+1}[n choose k+1]_q with [n choose 0]_q = 1 and [0 choose k+1]_q = 0. For a prime power q it counts the k-dimensional subspaces of F_qⁿ. It satisfies the q-binomial theorem ∏_{i=0}^{n−1}(1 + q^i X) = Σ_k q^{k(k−1)/2}[n choose k]_q X^k, and for every polynomial f of degree ≤ n − 1, Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2}[n choose i]_q f(q^{−i}) = 0.
hypotheses: q any integer for the recursion (the subspace count needs q a prime power).
k > n gives 0.
proofSteps: Define by the Pascal-type recursion on (n, k) in Z, so no division is needed.
Subspace count: count ordered bases of k-dimensional subspaces and divide by |GL_k(F_q)|; the recursion follows by splitting on whether the subspace lies in a fixed hyperplane.

The q-binomial theorem is proved by induction on n from the recursion; the alternating identity follows by applying it at X = −q^{−j}·(…) to the basis of polynomials ∏_{ℓ<j}(1 + q^{−ℓ}X) (HLSY Lemma 5.26 and Corollary 5.25).
acceptance: [n choose k]_1 is the ordinary binomial coefficient.
[4 choose 2]_2 = 35, the number of planes in F_2⁴.
[n choose k]_q = [n choose n − k]_q.

nodes.title: Orders of finite orthogonal groups
nodes.statement: Let q be an odd prime power and V a nondegenerate quadratic space of dimension m over F_q. Then |O(V)| = 2 q^{m(m−1)/2} (1 − sgn(V) q^{−m/2}) ∏_{1 ≤ i < m/2} (1 − q^{−2i}), where for even m, sgn(V) = ±1 according as V is split or not (χ((−1)^{m/2} det V)), and for odd m the factor (1 − sgn(V)q^{−m/2}) is omitted (sgn = 0). Equivalently |SO^±_{2r}(F_q)| = q^{r(r−1)}(q^r ∓ 1)∏_{i=1}^{r−1}(q^{2i} − 1) and |SO_{2r+1}(F_q)| = q^{r²}∏_{i=1}^r(q^{2i} − 1). For q a power of 2 the same formulas give the orders of the corresponding reductive (Chevalley and Steinberg) groups of types D_r, ²D_r and B_r, the last realized as the reductive quotient of the orthogonal group of an odd-dimensional form.
hypotheses: m ≥ 0; |O(0)| = 1 by convention (the product formula's 2 is replaced by 1 in dimension 0).
The split type is read from the signed determinant (−1)^{m/2} det V, not the plain determinant.
proofSteps: Induction on m by orbit–stabilizer for the action on vectors of a fixed nonzero norm (Witt's theorem), counting such vectors by Gauss sums: an m-dimensional nondegenerate form takes each nonzero value q^{m−1} − sgn·q^{(m−2)/2} times (m even) or q^{m−1} + χ(…)q^{(m−1)/2} times (m odd).
Collect the factors into the displayed product; the index [O:SO] = 2 in dimension ≥ 1.
For characteristic 2 cite the order formula of the finite groups of Lie type through the root datum (ReductiveGroups Layer 9 gives the split groups; the orders are Steinberg's formula).
acceptance: |O_2^+(F_3)| = 4 and |O_2^−(F_3)| = 8; the hyperbolic plane over F_3 has determinant −1, a nonsquare, yet is split: the signed determinant (−1)·(−1) = 1 is a square.

nodes.title: Isometries and isotropic subspaces of finite quadratic spaces
nodes.statement: Let q be odd, U a quadratic space of dimension n over F_q whose radical has dimension t, and V nondegenerate of dimension m ≥ n. The number #O(U,V) of injective isometries U → V is given by orbit–stabilizer from Witt's theorem: it is zero when U does not embed in V and otherwise equals, in the form of Li–Zhang Lemma 3.2.1, q^{n(2m−n−1)/2}(1 − sgn(V)q^{−m/2})(1 − χ(V)sgn_m(U)q^{−(m−n−t)/2})^{−1}∏_{(m−n−t)/2 ≤ i < m/2}(1 − q^{−2i}), read as the orbit–stabilizer count wherever the displayed rational expression is 0/0 (in particular U = 0 with m even, where the count is 1). The number S_b(V) of totally isotropic b-dimensional subspaces of V and the numbers m(U,V) of subspaces of V isometric to U are given by the same orbit–stabilizer argument (Li–Zhang Lemma 3.2.2; HLSY Lemmas 5.18–5.22).
hypotheses: q odd; injective isometries (embeddings) are counted, not all form-preserving maps.
The boundary case U = 0 has exactly one embedding; S_0(V) = 1.
proofSteps: Witt's theorem makes O(V) act transitively on embeddings of U with a given image type; the stabilizer of an embedding of U = U_0 ⊥ rad is computed from the orthogonal complement of the nondegenerate part and the parabolic fixing the isotropic radical.
Insert the orders of finite-orthogonal-group-order and the count of totally isotropic frames; simplify.
Subspace counts m(U,V) = #O(U,V)/(q^{jk}|O(U_0)|·|GL_j(F_q)|) (HLSY Lemma 5.18), and the flag identity of HLSY Lemma 5.22 from counting pairs of nested subspaces in two ways.

For U = 0 and m even the count is 1, while the printed rational expression of Li–Zhang Lemma 3.2.1 evaluates to 0/0 or a wrong value (their erratum E1).
For m = n = t = 1 (U a degenerate line, V a line) there is no embedding: a nondegenerate line has no isotropic vector.

nodes.title: Norm fibres of F_{q²}/F_q
nodes.statement: For a prime power q, the norm map N: F_{q²}^× → F_q^×, x ↦ x^{q+1}, is surjective and each fibre has q + 1 elements; the zero fibre {0} has one. Consequently the number of vectors of hermitian norm c in a nondegenerate hermitian space of dimension r over F_{q²} is q^{2r−1} − (−1)^r q^{r−1} for c ≠ 0 and q^{2r−1} + (−1)^r(q^r − q^{r−1}) for c = 0.
hypotheses: q a prime power, any characteristic.
proofSteps: The multiplicative group of F_{q²} is cyclic of order q² − 1, and x ↦ x^{q+1} has kernel of order q + 1 and image of order q − 1.
Diagonalize the hermitian form (every nondegenerate hermitian form over a finite field is isometric to the unit form) and count by induction on r.

nodes.title: Theta series of a positive definite lattice
nodes.statement: Let L be a positive definite integral Z-lattice (a TauCeti.IntegralLattice whose rational form B is positive definite). Its theta series is Θ_L(τ) = Σ_{x∈L} exp(πiτ B(x,x)) for τ in the upper half-plane. The sum converges absolutely and locally uniformly, Θ_L is holomorphic, and Θ_L(τ) = Σ_{m≥0} r_L(m) exp(πiτm) with r_L(m) = #{x ∈ L : B(x,x) = m} finite. For even L this is a power series in exp(2πiτ) with coefficients #{x : B(x,x)/2 = m}.
hypotheses: B positive definite and integral on L.
Modularity of Θ_L is not part of this construction.
proofSteps: Realize L in Euclidean space by the positive Gram form; finite-gauge-sublevel gives finiteness of each shell.
Bound #{x : B(x,x) ≤ T} ≤ C(1 + T)^{n/2} by a packing argument, so the series is dominated on Im τ ≥ y_0 > 0 by Σ_m C(1+m)^{n/2} e^{−π y_0 m}.
Weierstrass M-test gives local uniform convergence and holomorphy; regrouping the absolutely convergent sum by shells gives the coefficient formula.
acceptance: For L = Z with B(x,y) = xy, the coefficients of q⁰, q¹, q², q³, q⁴ (q = e^{πiτ}) are 1, 2, 0, 0, 2.
For L = Z² with the standard form, the coefficients of q and q² are 4 and 4.
The rank-zero lattice has Θ = 1.

nodes.title: Local representation densities of quadratic lattices
nodes.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic 0 with ring of integers O_F, uniformizer ϖ and residue cardinality q, and let M, L be nondegenerate quadratic O_F-lattices (integral quadratic lattices of GN.2 localized) of ranks m and n. The representation functor Rep_{M,L}(R) is the set of R-linear maps φ: L ⊗ R → M ⊗ R with Q_M ∘ φ = Q_L, for O_F-algebras R; it is represented by an affine O_F-scheme of finite type. When its generic fibre is nonempty (then n ≤ m), the generic fibre has dimension d = n(2m − n − 1)/2, and the local density is Den(M,L) = lim_N #Rep_{M,L}(O_F/ϖ^N)/q^{N d}. When the generic fibre is empty, Den(M,L) = 0. The representation density of an element t ∈ O_F by M is the case L = ⟨t⟩ (rank one, Q_L(x) = t x²): β(M,t) = lim_N q^{−N(m−1)}#{v ∈ M/ϖ^N M : Q_M(v) ≡ t mod ϖ^N}.
hypotheses: Quadratic maps are primary: Q_M ∘ φ = Q_L, which for p = 2 is stronger than equality of the polar bilinear forms.
The density is the eventual value of the normalized counts (density-stabilization), not a chosen limit.
Basis changes of M and L act on Rep_{M,L} by isomorphisms.
proofSteps: Write Rep_{M,L} in bases: X ∈ M_{m×n} with the n(n+1)/2 equations Q_M(Xe_i) = Q_L(e_i) and polar equations for i < j; this is a closed subscheme of affine space.
Generic dimension: over F, Rep is a torsor-type fibration O_m → O_m/O_{m−n}, giving dim O_m − dim O_{m−n}.

Define the density as the eventual value of the normalized sequence (quadratic-density-stabilization), with the empty generic fibre giving 0 by the eventual-emptiness argument of the parent node empty-generic-density-zero transported to the quadratic case.
Compatibility: for F = Q_p, p odd, and M = L, Den(L,L) is the automorphism density α_p(L) of IntegralLattices 7C (same count and same exponent n(n−1)/2).

For M = ⟨1⟩ and t = p: β = 0 for p odd, although x = 0 solves x² ≡ p mod p.

nodes.title: Stabilization of quadratic representation counts
nodes.statement: In the setting of quadratic-local-density with nonempty generic fibre, there is N_0, depending on n, m and the valuations of the discriminants of M and L and of 2, such that #Rep_{M,L}(O_F/ϖ^{N+1}) = q^d #Rep_{M,L}(O_F/ϖ^N) for all N ≥ N_0; when the generic fibre is empty the counts vanish for N ≥ N_0. For representation numbers of a maximal Z_p-lattice of rank r ≥ 5, the normalized counts μ_p(m,n) are constant for n ≥ w_p(m), where w_p(m) = 1 + v_p(m) for p odd and w_2(m) = 1 + 2v_2(2m), and |μ_p(m,n) − μ_p(m,w_p(m))| ≪ p^{−(3⌊n/2⌋−2)} for 2 + v_2(p) ≤ n < w_p(m), with an absolute implied constant.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0; for the quantitative part, L a maximal Z_p-lattice of rank r ≥ 5 and m ≠ 0.
proofSteps: The integral solution set of Q_M∘X = Q_L is compact; near each solution the Jacobian of the Gram map has a right inverse with denominators bounded by the valuations of 2 det, so a quadratic Hensel lemma gives finitely many residue charts on which the map is a submersion after fixed scalings (the quadratic analogue of the parent node's hermitian stabilization argument).
On each chart every additional level adds exactly q^d points; compactness shows all sufficiently accurate approximate solutions lie in the charts.
Empty generic fibre: a convergent subsequence of approximate solutions would give an exact solution, so the counts vanish eventually.
Quantitative part: SSTT Corollary 4.3 expresses μ_p(m,n) through good-type densities at level 1 and the reduction maps, which gives the stated decay (SSTT Lemma 4.4).
acceptance: For M = ⟨1⟩ over Z_3 and t = 1 the normalized counts are 2 from N = 1 on.
For M = ⟨1⟩ and t = 9 over Z_3 (rank one, so the normalizing exponent is 0): the counts modulo 3, 9, 27, 81 are 1, 3, 6, 6, stabilizing from N = 3 = 1 + v_3(9).
Empty generic fibre: x² = 3 over Z_3 has a solution modulo 3 but none modulo 9.

nodes.title: Jordan splitting and Hanke's solution types
nodes.statement: Let L_p be a maximal quadratic Z_p-lattice of rank r. Fix a Jordan splitting L_p = ⊕_j (L_j, p^{ν_j}Q_j) with each (L_j,Q_j) unimodular of rank 1 (p odd) or rank 1 or 2 (p = 2); maximality forces ν_j ∈ {0,1}. Put S_i = {j : ν_j = i} and s_i = Σ_{j∈S_i} rank L_j (total rank, not the number of blocks), and let Q′ be the form with each ν_j replaced by 1 − ν_j. A solution v of Q(v) ≡ m mod p^n is of zero type if v ≡ 0 mod p, of good type if v_j ≢ 0 mod p for some j with ν_j = 0, and of bad type otherwise. This splits the count N_m(p^n) = N_m^good + N_m^bad + N_m^zero and the densities μ_p = μ^good + μ^bad + μ^zero accordingly.
hypotheses: L maximal (for ν_j ≤ 1); r ≥ 1.
The types depend on the chosen splitting only through the decomposition into the ν = 0 and ν = 1 parts.
proofSteps: Existence of the Jordan splitting with blocks of rank ≤ 2 is IntegralLattices 3B–3C over Z_p (and GN.2 dyadic-atomic-form in general).
Maximality: a block with ν_j ≥ 2 would allow the overlattice p^{−1}L_j, contradicting maximality.
The three types partition the solution set; the densities are the normalized counts of each type.
acceptance: For p ∤ m every solution modulo p is of good type, so N_m = N_m^good.
If p² ∤ m and n ≥ 2 there are no zero-type solutions.
If p ∤ 2 det L there are no bad-type solutions (all ν_j = 0).

nodes.title: Hanke's reduction maps for local densities
nodes.statement: Let L be a maximal Z_p-lattice of rank r with the data of hanke-solution-types and δ = 2v_2(p) + 1. (1) For n ≥ δ and all m, μ^good_p(m,n) = μ^good_p(m,δ). (2) If p | m, then N^bad_{m,Q}(p^{n+1}) = p^{r−s_0}N^good_{m/p,Q′}(p^n), equivalently μ^bad_{p,Q}(m,n+1) = p^{1−s_0}μ^good_{p,Q′}(m/p,n). (3) If p² | m, then N^zero_m(p^{n+2}) = p^r N_{m/p²}(p^n), equivalently μ^zero_p(m,n+2) = p^{2−r}μ_p(m/p², n). Here n ≥ 1 and s_0 is a total rank, also at p = 2.
hypotheses: L maximal; n ≥ 1.
proofSteps: (1) Good-type solutions are smooth points of the quadric modulo p (a coordinate in a unimodular block is a unit), so Hensel's lemma lifts each solution modulo p^n to exactly p^{r−1} solutions modulo p^{n+1} once n ≥ δ.

(2) A bad-type v has its ν = 0 coordinates divisible by p; substituting v = (pw_0, w_1) gives p·Q′(w) ≡ m mod p^{n+1}, and the free choices of the ν = 0 coordinates modulo p^{n+1} contribute p^{r − s_0}.
(3) Zero-type v = pw gives p²Q(w) ≡ m mod p^{n+2}, with p^r choices of w modulo p^{n+1} over each w modulo p^n.
acceptance: For Q = ab + cd + 2t² and m = 2 at p = 2: bad counts modulo 4 and 8 are 32 and 640, good Q′ norm-one counts modulo 2 and 4 are 16 and 320, and the factor 2^{5−4} = 2 matches both (s_0 = 4).
For a unimodular L and p odd, (2) is vacuous: there are no bad solutions.

sources.match: States the three reduction identities, attributed to Hanke, with the rank convention corrected (E7).
Uses them to compute the densities at odd p.

nodes.title: Closed formulas for densities at odd primes
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, L a maximal Z_p-lattice of rank r, and δ_{p,det L} = 1 if p | det L and 0 otherwise. (1) If n ≥ v_p(m) + 1, then μ_{p,Q}(m,n) = Σ_{u=0}^{⌊v_p(m)/2⌋} p^{(2−r)u} μ^good_{p,Q}(m/p^{2u},1) + δ_{p,det L} p^{1−s_0} Σ_{u=0}^{⌊(v_p(m)−1)/2⌋} p^{(2−r)u} μ^good_{p,Q′}(m/p^{2u+1},1). (2) If 1 ≤ n ≤ v_p(m) and n is odd, μ_{p,Q}(m,n) = p^{(2−r)(n−1)/2}μ_{p,Q}(mp^{1−n},1) + Σ_{u=0}^{(n−3)/2} p^{(2−r)u}μ^good_{p,Q}(m/p^{2u},1) + δ_{p,det L}p^{1−s_0}Σ_{u=0}^{(n−3)/2}p^{(2−r)u}μ^good_{p,Q′}(m/p^{2u+1},1), and (3) the analogous formula holds for n even. The level-one good densities are explicit point counts of nondegenerate quadrics over F_p.
hypotheses: p odd; L maximal; m ≠ 0.
proofSteps: Iterate hanke-reduction-maps, splitting each count into its three types, until the level is one or the remaining part of m is prime to p.
Use (1) of the reduction maps to replace good densities at higher level by level one (δ = 1 for odd p).
The level-one good densities are counts of smooth points of a quadric over F_p (finite-orthogonal-group-order and its Gauss-sum vector counts).
acceptance: Q = x_1x_2 + x_3x_4 + 3x_5² at p = 3, n = 3: formula (1) agrees with direct counts for every m < 27.
For L unimodular (δ = 0) and p ∤ m, μ_p(m,n) = μ^good_p(m,1) for all n ≥ 1.
At m with v_p(m) = 1 the second sum in (1) has the single term u = 0.

sources.match: Gives the closed formulas for μ_p(m,n) at odd p in terms of level-one good densities of Q and Q′.

nodes.title: Densities near one at good primes and a uniform lower bound
nodes.statement: Let L be a positive definite maximal Z-lattice of rank r ≥ 5. (1) There is C > 0 such that |μ_p(m,n) − 1| ≤ C/p for all m, n ≥ 1 and all primes p ∤ 2 det L. (2) μ_p(m,n) ≥ 1/2 for all m, n ≥ 1 and all primes p.
hypotheses: r ≥ 5 and L maximal for (2); (1) needs only p ∤ 2 det L.
proofSteps: (1) By odd-prime-density-formula, μ_p(m,n) is a short combination of level-one densities; for a nondegenerate quadric in r ≥ 5 variables over F_p, the number of solutions of Q(x) = c is p^{r−1} + O(p^{r/2}), by Gauss sums, so each level-one density is 1 + O(p^{−3/2}) (or 1 + O(1/p) at the zero class), and the extra terms carry factors p^{2−r}.

(2) A maximal lattice of rank ≥ 5 has a hyperbolic plane over Z_p: Q = x_1x_2 + Q_1 in a suitable basis. Solutions with x_1 a unit are good and number at least (p−1)/p of the maximum, giving μ^good ≥ (p−1)/p ≥ 1/2.
acceptance: For a unimodular form of rank 5, p odd and p ∤ m, μ_p(m,1) = p^{−4}#{x ∈ F_p^5 : Q(x) = m} = 1 + χ(m det Q)p^{−2}.
Without the rank and maximality hypotheses the lower bound fails: for ⟨1⟩ and p odd, μ_p(p,n) = 0 for n ≥ 2.
At p = 2 the bound (2) still holds for maximal lattices of rank ≥ 5.

nodes.title: Bounds for the local terms in Bruinier–Kühn and for discriminant-sensitive densities
nodes.statement: Let L be a positive definite maximal Z-lattice of rank r ≥ 5. (1) If m is represented by L over Z, then |w_p(m) − Σ_{n=0}^{w_p(m)−1} μ_p(m,n)/μ_p(m,w_p(m))| ≪ 1/p with an implied constant independent of p and m. (2) For every positive definite integral quadratic form Q of rank r ≥ 5, m ≥ 1 and prime p, μ_∞(Q,1)μ_p(Q,m) ≪_r p^r/|Disc Q|^{3/20}, where μ_∞(Q,1) ≍_r Disc(Q)^{−1/2} is the archimedean density.
hypotheses: r ≥ 5; (1) for maximal L, (2) for arbitrary positive definite integral Q.
proofSteps: (1) For p ∤ 2 det L, combine density-good-prime-bounds (1) at every level n < w_p(m); for p | 2 det L, use quadratic-density-stabilization's decay and the lower bound 1/2.

(2) Decompose μ_p into good, two bad and zero parts (Hanke); bound μ^good ≤ p³, the first bad part ≤ p⁴, and the second bad and zero parts by p^{2−r} times densities of forms of smaller discriminant at level n − 2, then induct on n using Disc(Q″) ≥ Disc(Q)/p^{2r}.
acceptance: For p ∤ 2 det L and p ∤ m, w_p(m) = 1 and the term in (1) is |1 − μ_p(m,0)/μ_p(m,1)| = |1 − 1/μ_p(m,1)| = O(1/p).
(2) is vacuous in rank < 5: the proof uses the archimedean factor's exponent and r ≥ 5.
The exponent 3/20 is the paper's; no sharper exponent is claimed.

sources.match: Bounds the local term of the Bruinier–Kühn formula by O(1/p).
Proves the discriminant-sensitive bound by induction on the level using Hanke's decomposition.

nodes.title: Cho–Yamauchi formula for quadratic densities
nodes.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with odd residue characteristic, L a nondegenerate quadratic O_F-lattice of rank n, and H^ε_m the self-dual quadratic O_F-lattice of rank m ≥ n whose reduction has χ = ε (for odd m, ε is the sign of the discriminant class). For an integral overlattice L′ ⊇ L let t(L′) = dim_k(L′^∨/L′ ⊗ k) be its type and sgn_m(L′) the sign of the nondegenerate part of the reduction of L′ (LZ (3.2.0.6)). Then Den(H^ε_m, L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} q^{(n+1−m)ℓ(L′/L)}(1 − sgn(H^ε_m)q^{−m/2})(1 + ε sgn_m(L′)q^{−(m−n−t(L′))/2})∏_{(m−n−t(L′))/2 < i < m/2}(1 − q^{−2i}) (Li–Zhang (3.3.2.1)); the summand indexed by L′ is the normalized number of isometries of the reduction of L′ into that of H^ε_m, times the volume factor q^{(n+1−m)ℓ(L′/L)}.
hypotheses: Odd residue characteristic; the sum is over integral lattices L′ with L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨, finite because L′ ⊆ L^∨.
proofSteps: Every representation of L extends uniquely to a primitive representation of its saturation L′ (an integral overlattice); this partitions Rep(H^ε_m, L) by L′.
Primitive representations of L′ are smooth points; their density is q^{−d} times the finite-field isometry count of the reductions (orthogonal-isometry-count).
The change of variables from L to L′ contributes q^{(n+1−m)ℓ(L′/L)}.
acceptance: For n = 0 the sum has one term and Den(H^ε_m, 0) = 1.
For L = H^ε_n self-dual and m = n, the sum has the single term L′ = L and Den(H^ε_n, H^ε_n) = q^{−n(n−1)/2}|O(H^ε_n ⊗ k)|, the normalized finite orthogonal group order.
The rank-one case L = ⟨ϖ^a⟩ gives a finite sum over the overlattices ⟨ϖ^{a−2j}⟩.

sources.match: Proves the weighted lattice-count formula for Den(H^ε_m, L) from Cho–Yamauchi's method and Lemma 3.2.1, and the induction formula of Lemma 3.3.3.
The finite-field isometry count that gives each summand.

nodes.title: Normalized local Siegel series of quadratic lattices
nodes.statement: For a quadratic O_F-lattice L of rank n (odd residue characteristic) and ε = ±1: (odd corank) Den^ε(X,L) ∈ Z[X] is the unique polynomial with Den^ε(q^{−k},L) = Den(H^ε_{n+1+2k},L)/Den(H^ε_{n+1+2k},H^ε_n) for all k ≥ 0; it equals Σ_{L⊆L′⊆L′^∨} X^{2ℓ(L′/L)} m^ε(t(L′), sgn_{n+1}(L′); X) with m(t,s;X) = (1 + s q^{(t−1)/2}X)∏_{0≤i<(t−1)/2}(1 − q^{2i}X²) and m^ε(t,s;X) = m(t,s;εX). (Even corank) Den^{♭ε}(X,L) is defined by Den^{♭ε}(q^{−k},L) = Den(H^ε_{n+2k},L)/Nor^{♭ε}(q^{−k},L) and equals Σ_{L′}(q^{1/2}X)^{2ℓ(L′/L)}m^{♭ε}(t(L′),sgn_n(L′),χ(L);X), with m^♭(t,s,χ;X) = (1 + s q^{t/2}X)(1 − χX)∏_{0<i<t/2}(1 − q^{2i}X²) for t > 0 and m^♭ = 1 for t = 0. The central derivative ∂Den^ε(L) = −(d/dX)Den^ε(X,L)|_{X=1} is defined when Den^ε(1,L) = 0.
hypotheses: Odd residue characteristic; L nondegenerate; the normalizing polynomials Nor^ε, Nor^{♭ε} depend only on n (and χ(L) for the even case).
proofSteps: Apply orthogonal-cho-yamauchi with m = n + 1 + 2k (resp. n + 2k) and divide by the self-dual value; each summand becomes the stated weight polynomial evaluated at q^{−k}.
The finite sum defines the polynomial; agreement at infinitely many points gives uniqueness.
acceptance: For L self-dual of rank n, Den^ε(X,L) = 1 (only L′ = L, type 0).
For the lattice with invariants (1,1,1) in the case m = 4, ε = −1: Den^−(X,L) = 1 − qX + qX² − X³ and ∂Den^−(L) = 3 − q.
The weight m^♭(0,s,χ;X) is 1, not (1 + sX)(1 − χX).

nodes.title: Functional equations of the orthogonal Siegel series (Ikeda)
nodes.statement: For a quadratic O_F-lattice L of rank n (odd residue characteristic): Den^ε(X,L) = w^ε(L)X^{val(L)}Den^ε(1/X,L) with w^ε(L) = (det L, −(−1)^{n(n+1)/2}u)_F ϵ(L_F) (a Hilbert symbol times the Hasse invariant), and Den^{♭ε}(X,L) = (q^{1/2}X)^{2⌊val(L)/2⌋}Den^{♭ε}(1/(qX),L). In particular, if w^ε(L) = −1 then Den^ε(1,L) = 0 and ∂Den^ε(L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} m^ε(t(L′), sgn_{n+1}(L′)), where m^ε(t,s) = −(d/dX)m^ε(t,s;X)|_{X=1}.

proofSteps: Ikeda's theorem [Ike17, Thm 4.1(2)] in the case n odd, ε = +1; the same proof gives the general case (Li–Zhang Theorem 3.4.6).

nodes.title: Induction formula for the orthogonal Siegel series
nodes.statement: Let L^♭ be an integral quadratic lattice of rank n − 1 with last fundamental invariant a_{n−1}, x ⊥ L^♭ with val(x) > a_{n−1}, L = L^♭ ⊥ ⟨x⟩ and L̃ = L^♭ ⊥ ⟨ϖ^{−1}x⟩. With A = Den^ε(X,L), B = Den^ε(X,L̃), D = Den^{♭ε}(X,L^♭) and c = εχ(L^♭): A(X) = X²B(X) + (1 − X²)D(X)/(1 − cX). If w^ε(L) = −1, then ∂Den^ε(L) − ∂Den^ε(L̃) = 2D(1) when c = 0, D(1) when c = −1, and −2D′(1) when c = +1 (in which case D(1) = 0).
hypotheses: Odd residue characteristic; L^♭ integral and nondegenerate.
proofSteps: Partition the overlattices of L in the weighted sum of orthogonal-siegel-series by their intersection with L^♭_F and compare with those of L̃ (Li–Zhang Theorem 3.6.1, generalizing Katsurada's induction).
Differentiate at X = 1 using A(1) = B(1) = 0; the three cases come from the factor (1 − X²)/(1 − cX).
The printed Corollary 3.6.2 omits the derivative term when c = +1; the corrected statement is the one above (recorded as GN/E301).
acceptance: For c = 0: (1 − X²) has derivative −2 at X = 1, giving 2D(1).
For c = −1: (1 − X²)/(1 + X) = 1 − X, giving D(1).
For c = +1: (1 − X²)/(1 − X) = 1 + X and D(1) = 0, giving −2D′(1); the printed formula's D(1)-term is 0 here and misses this.

nodes.title: Co-isotropic and horizontal lattices
nodes.statement: Let V^ε_m be the quadratic space of dimension m = n + 1 attached to ε and L^♭ ⊆ V^ε_m an O_F-lattice of rank n − 1. L^♭ is co-isotropic if the orthogonal complement (L^♭_F)^⊥ is isotropic, equivalently χ(L^♭) = ε; otherwise co-anisotropic. L^♭ is horizontal if it is integral and either t(L^♭) ≤ 1, or t(L^♭) = 2 and ε·sgn_{n−1}(L^♭) = +1. Hor^ε(L^♭) is the set of horizontal M^♭ ⊇ L^♭ in L^♭_F.
hypotheses: Odd residue characteristic; rank n − 1 lattices in an n + 1-dimensional space.
proofSteps: Define the predicates from the invariants χ, t and sgn of the reduction.

Corollary 3.8.3 of Li–Zhang: for co-isotropic L^♭, Den^{♭ε}(1,L^♭) = 0 and Hor^ε(L^♭) = ∅; for co-anisotropic L^♭ the derivative difference of orthogonal-induction-formula is a weighted count of Hor^ε(L^♭) with weights q^{⌊val(M^♭)/2⌋}·(1, 1 + q^{−1}, 2(1 + q^{−1})) by type 0, 1, 2.
Lemma 3.8.4: a lattice embedding in both V^ε_m and H^ε_m with M^♭ = M^♭_F ∩ H^ε_m is horizontal.

A lattice of type 3 is never horizontal.
A type-2 lattice is horizontal for exactly one of the two signs ε.

nodes.statement: Let L^♭ be an integral quadratic lattice of rank n − 1 with fundamental invariants (a_1,…,a_{n−1}) and x ∈ Ω(L^♭) (the vectors with L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ nondegenerate of rank n). nodes.title: Weighted counting identities for full-type lattices
nodes.statement: Let L be a quadratic O_F-lattice of rank t and full type t > 1 (t(L) = t, i.e. every fundamental invariant is positive), and μ_+(L) = #(ϖL^∨)°°/L, μ_0(L) = #((ϖL^∨)° ∖ (ϖL^∨)°°)/L, μ_−(L) = #((L^∨)° ∖ (ϖL^∨)°)/L, where X° = {x : val(x) ≥ 0} and X°° = {x : val(x) > 0}; μ_{0,s} refines μ_0 by the sign s of χ(⟨x⟩_F) (χ(L) = 0) or of χ(⟨x⟩^⊥_F) (χ(L) ≠ 0). Then μ_+ + μ_0 + μ_− = q^{t−1}μ_+ for the relative counts μ_?(L,M) = μ_?(L) − [M:L]μ_?(M) over L ⊆ M ⊆ ϖ^{−1}L (Li–Zhang Lemma 8.2.3), and, for t odd, (1 − q^{t−1})μ_+ + (1 − sq^{(t−1)/2})μ_{0,+} + (1 + sq^{(t−1)/2})μ_{0,−} + μ_− = 0 when χ(L) = 0 (s = ±1) or χ(L) ≠ 0 and s = +1; for t even, (1 − sq^{t/2})(1 + sq^{t/2−1})μ_+ + (1 + sq^{t/2−1})μ_0 + μ_− = 0 when χ(L) = 0 (s = ±1) or χ(L) = s. The helper existence statements of Lemmas 8.2.4 and 8.2.6 are used only under the additional hypothesis a_t ≥ 3.
hypotheses: Odd residue characteristic; full type t > 1.
The unrestricted existence claims of Lemmas 8.2.4/8.2.6 are false in general (paper erratum E10, failures for diag(3,3,9), diag(3,3), diag(9,9) over Z_3).
proofSteps: Lemma 8.2.3 by counting vectors of each valuation class modulo L.

Propositions 8.2.5 and 8.2.7 by induction on val(L) from the maximal (type-t self-dual-up-to-scaling) lattices, using an index-q overlattice M with the stated relative identity; the induction step uses the helper lemmas, available when a_t ≥ 3, and the base cases directly.
The full induction in the cases excluded by E10 is a recorded gap of this node.
acceptance: At the maximal lattices the identities reduce to (1 − qa)(1 + a) + (1 + a)(q − 1) + q^t − q = 0 with a² = q^{t−1}.

nodes.title: Siegel's main theorem for positive definite forms
nodes.statement: Let L be a positive definite integral Z-lattice of rank n ≥ 5 with quadratic form Q (Q(x) = B(x,x)/2 integral). Then for every integer m ≥ 1 the genus representation number of genus-theta-average satisfies r_gen(L,m) = β_∞(L,m)·∏_p β(L ⊗ Z_p, m), where β(L ⊗ Z_p, m) are the local representation densities of quadratic-local-density and β_∞(L,m) = (π^{n/2}/Γ(n/2)) m^{n/2−1} det(L)^{−1/2} is the archimedean density (with det taken for the Gram matrix of Q's polar form divided by 2). The Euler product converges absolutely. Equivalently, the genus theta average is the Eisenstein part of Θ_L.
hypotheses: n ≥ 5 (absolute convergence of the Euler product and of the Eisenstein series); positive definite.
The left side is the mass-weighted genus average, not the representation number of L itself.
proofSteps: Proved by Siegel (1935) through the circle method and, in the representation-theoretic form, by Weil's Siegel–Weil formula; here the route is rank-one-siegel-weil applied to the characteristic function of the adelic closure of L, unfolded over the finite class set (adelic-mass-identity of the parent packet).
The Fourier coefficient of the Eisenstein distribution at m is the product of the local fibre integrals, which are the densities β_p and β_∞.
Absolute convergence: density-good-prime-bounds gives β_p = 1 + O(p^{−3/2})·… for p ∤ 2 det L and n ≥ 5.
acceptance: For Q = x² + y² + z² + w² + t² (n = 5, one class) the formula gives r_{Z^5}(m) exactly.
For the sum of four squares (n = 4, outside the hypothesis) Jacobi's formula r(m) = 8Σ_{4∤d|m} d agrees with the product of local densities computed in Hanke's §2.7.
For a two-class genus in rank ≥ 5 the identity holds for the weighted average and generally fails for each class separately.

sources.match: States Siegel's theorem for positive definite forms in n ≥ 5 variables: the Eisenstein part is the mass-weighted genus average and its coefficients are products of local densities; §2.7 works the sum of four squares.
Applies the formula to the auxiliary lattices with explicit L-values; see mst-auxiliary-mass-formula.

nodes.title: Siegel's formula for the Maulik–Shankar–Tang auxiliary lattices
nodes.statement: Let L′_1 be the positive definite auxiliary lattice of rank b + 2 of Maulik–Shankar–Tang, maximal away from p, and L′ ⊆ L′_1 with the same Z_ℓ-localizations for ℓ ≠ p; put d′ = |L′^∨/L′|, Δ_1 = det L′_1 and C_b(m) the archimedean factor. For even b, with χ′ = χ_{(−1)^{1+b/2}4Δ_1}, the genus representation number is q_{L′}(m) = C_b(m)σ_{−b/2}(m,χ′)/(√d′ L(1 + b/2, χ′))·∏_{ℓ|2Δ_1}δ(ℓ,L′,m). For odd b, writing m = m_0 f² with (f, 2Δ_1) = 1 and v_ℓ(m_0) ∈ {0,1} for ℓ ∤ 2Δ_1, and D′ = (−1)^{(b−1)/2}2m_0Δ_1: q_{L′}(m) = C_b(m)L((b+1)/2, χ_{D′})/(√d′ ζ(b+1))·[Σ_{a|f}μ(a)χ_{D′}(a)a^{−(b+1)/2}σ_{−b}(f/a)]·∏_{ℓ|2Δ_1}δ(ℓ,L′,m)/(1 − ℓ^{−1−b}).
hypotheses: b ≥ 3 (rank ≥ 5); the character D′ is used in both the L-value and the divisor sum.
proofSteps: Apply siegel-main-theorem and evaluate the good-prime densities by odd-prime-density-formula: for ℓ ∤ 2Δ_1 they are Euler factors of the displayed divisor sums and L-values.
Collect the factors at ℓ | 2Δ_1 as the remaining densities δ(ℓ,L′,m).
acceptance: For even b and m = 1 the divisor sum is 1 and q_{L′}(1) = C_b(1)/(√d′L(1 + b/2,χ′))·∏_{ℓ|2Δ_1}δ(ℓ,L′,1).
χ_{D} and χ_{D′} agree on the divisors of f allowed in the sum, so the printed χ_D is not an error.
Comparing with the same formula for L (Theorem 7.4) term by term gives MST Lemma 7.16.

nodes.title: The hermitian representation scheme and its primitive open
nodes.statement: For hermitian O_F-lattices L (rank n) and M (rank m), Rep_{M,L} is the O_{F_0}-scheme with Rep_{M,L}(S) = {O_F ⊗ S-linear φ : L ⊗ S → M ⊗ S preserving the hermitian forms} for O_{F_0}-algebras S. In bases it is cut out of affine space of dimension 2mn over O_{F_0} by the n² real equations of XᴴGX = B. Its primitive open Rep^prim_{M,L} is the locus where some n × n minor of X is a unit. If the generic fibre is nonempty then n ≤ m and it is smooth of dimension n(2m − n). Points over O_{F_0}/ϖ^N are counted by the parent node hermitian-representation-count applied to the reductions of the Gram matrices.
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).
Hermitian lattices are integral hermitian O_F-lattices of the parent node GN.2 integral-hermitian-lattice; ⟨1⟩^k is the self-dual lattice of rank k.
proofSteps: Write the functor in coordinates of O_F ⊗ S ≅ S² (unramified basis), giving polynomial equations in 2mn variables.
Generic dimension: over F_0 the scheme is a U_m-torsor quotient U_m/U_{m−n}, of dimension m² − (m − n)² = n(2m − n).
Smoothness on the generic fibre: the derivative Y ↦ XᴴGY + YᴴGX is onto the hermitian matrices, since Y = XB^{−1}H/2 maps to H (division by 2 over the characteristic-0 field).
The primitive open is defined by the nonvanishing of an n × n minor modulo ϖ.
acceptance: Rank-zero source: the terminal scheme, with one primitive point at every level.
A rank-one zero Gram source has the zero representation, which lies outside the primitive open.
Over F_4/F_2 the rank-one unit Gram matrices have three primitive points (the norm-one elements).

nodes.title: Stabilization of hermitian representation counts
nodes.statement: For integral nondegenerate hermitian lattices L, M of ranks n ≤ m over an unramified F/F_0 with nonempty generic representation fibre, there is N_0 such that #Rep_{M,L}(O_{F_0}/ϖ^{N+1}) = q^{n(2m−n)}#Rep_{M,L}(O_{F_0}/ϖ^N) for all N ≥ N_0. Consequently the normalized counts of the parent node normalized-hermitian-count are eventually constant, and their eventual value is the density of the parent node hermitian-local-density.
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).
Hermitian lattices are integral hermitian O_F-lattices of the parent node GN.2 integral-hermitian-lattice; ⟨1⟩^k is the self-dual lattice of rank k.
proofSteps: The set of exact integral solutions is compact.

At every exact solution the Jacobian of the Gram map has a right inverse with denominators bounded in terms of v(2) and v(det B); a multivariate quadratic Hensel lemma gives finitely many residue charts on which the map is a submersion after fixed scalings.
Each chart contributes exactly q^{n(2m−n)} more points per level; compactness shows that all sufficiently accurate approximate solutions lie in the charts.
The empty-generic case is the parent node empty-generic-density-zero.
acceptance: m = n = 1, M = L = ⟨1⟩: the counts are q + 1 at every level N ≥ 1 multiplied by q^{N−1}, so the normalized count is (q+1)/q from N = 1.
For n = 0 the count is 1 at every level.
Generic smoothness alone does not give the count identity at small N: for M = ⟨1⟩, L = ⟨ϖ²⟩ the normalized counts at N = 1, 2, 3 are not all equal.

sources.match: Defines the density as a limit and records the generic dimension; stabilization is the input that makes the limit an eventual value.

nodes.title: Primitive representations into a self-dual lattice
nodes.statement: For the self-dual target I_m = ⟨1⟩^m and an integral hermitian lattice L of rank n ≤ m over an unramified F/F_0 (residue characteristic 2 included), the primitive representation scheme Rep^prim_{I_m,L} is smooth over O_{F_0} of relative dimension d = n(2m − n). Hence #Rep^prim(O_{F_0}/ϖ^N) = q^{(N−1)d}·#Emb(L ⊗ k, I_m ⊗ k), and the primitive density Den_prim(I_m, L) equals q^{−d} times the finite-field embedding count of the parent node hermitian-embedding-count.
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).
Hermitian lattices are integral hermitian O_F-lattices of the parent node GN.2 integral-hermitian-lattice; ⟨1⟩^k is the self-dual lattice of rank k.
proofSteps: On the special fibre, injectivity of X and nondegeneracy of the target make Y ↦ XᴴY onto all n × n matrices.
A ↦ A + Aᴴ is onto the hermitian matrices over k_F, the diagonal being supplied by the surjective trace k_F → k_{F_0} of the unramified extension (this replaces division by 2 and works at p = 2).
Lift the surjectivity over O_{F_0} and apply the Jacobian criterion; smoothness gives the point count by Hensel.
acceptance: n = 0: one point at every level.
m = n = 1 over F_4/F_2: 3 primitive points at level one.
Over a ramified extension the trace map on residue fields is zero, so this argument fails; the ramified case needs ramified-primitive-density.

nodes.title: Saturation decomposition of hermitian densities
nodes.statement: For the self-dual target I_m and an integral hermitian lattice L of rank n ≤ m over an unramified F/F_0: every representation of L extends uniquely to a primitive representation of its saturation L′, an integral overlattice L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨, and Den(I_m, L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} q^{−2(m−n)ℓ(L′/L)}Den_prim(I_m, L′), where ℓ is the O_F-length. The sum is finite because L′ ⊆ L^∨.
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).
Hermitian lattices are integral hermitian O_F-lattices of the parent node GN.2 integral-hermitian-lattice; ⟨1⟩^k is the self-dual lattice of rank k.
proofSteps: Saturation: the image of L under φ is contained in a unique primitive sublattice of rank n; its preimage is L′ and φ is primitive on L′.
Change of variables: on Hom coordinates passing from L to L′ multiplies volume by q^{−2mℓ}, on hermitian-form coordinates by q^{2nℓ}.
Interchange the finite sum with the stabilized counts (hermitian-count-stabilizes).
acceptance: For L self-dual, only L′ = L occurs.
For L = ⟨ϖ^a⟩ of rank one, the overlattices are ⟨ϖ^{a−2j}⟩ for 0 ≤ 2j ≤ a.
Combining with primitive-hermitian-smooth-count gives the Cho–Yamauchi formula of the parent node.

nodes.title: Cancellation law for hermitian densities
nodes.statement: For a self-dual hermitian lattice M of rank m and an integral hermitian lattice L^♭ of rank n over an unramified F/F_0: Den(⟨1⟩^{n+m+k}, L^♭ ⊕ M) = Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, L^♭) for all k ≥ 0, hence the normalized Siegel polynomials agree: D_{L^♭ ⊕ M}(X) = D_{L^♭}(X).
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).
Hermitian lattices are integral hermitian O_F-lattices of the parent node GN.2 integral-hermitian-lattice; ⟨1⟩^k is the self-dual lattice of rank k.
proofSteps: Representations of M into a self-dual target split off: the orthogonal complement of the image of M is self-dual of rank n + k, and the stabilizer count cancels against the self-dual denominator.
Alternatively, the overlattices of L^♭ ⊕ M are L′ ⊕ M (M self-dual), with the same type and length, so the Cho–Yamauchi sums agree.
acceptance: L^♭ = 0: D_M(X) = 1 for every self-dual M.
The cancellation fails for a non-self-dual M: D_{⟨ϖ⟩⊕⟨ϖ⟩}(X) ≠ D_{⟨ϖ⟩}(X).

sources.match: States the cancellation law for densities against self-dual targets and for the normalized Siegel series.

nodes.title: Central derivative of the hermitian Siegel series
nodes.statement: For an integral nondegenerate hermitian lattice L over an unramified F/F_0 with normalized Siegel polynomial D_L(X) (parent node normalized-siegel-polynomial), put Den(L) = D_L(1) and, when val(L) is odd (so that D_L(1) = 0 by the functional equation), ∂Den(L) = −(d/dX)D_L(X)|_{X=1}. Then ∂Den(L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} m(t(L′)) with m(a) = ∏_{i=1}^{a−1}(1 − (−q)^i) for a ≥ 1 and m(0) = 0, every L′ in the sum having t(L′) > 0 and val(L′) ≡ val(L) mod 2. For rank one, D_L(X) = Σ_{i=0}^{val L}(−X)^i, and ∂Den(L) = (val(L) + 1)/2 for odd val(L).
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).
Hermitian lattices are integral hermitian O_F-lattices of the parent node GN.2 integral-hermitian-lattice; ⟨1⟩^k is the self-dual lattice of rank k.
∂Den is defined only for odd val(L).
proofSteps: Differentiate the Cho–Yamauchi formula of the parent node at X = 1: the factor X^{2ℓ} contributes nothing because m(t;1) = 0 for t ≥ 1, and m(0;X) = 1 is constant.
If val(L) is odd, every integral overlattice has odd valuation and hence positive type.
Rank one: the overlattices of ⟨ϖ^a⟩ are ⟨ϖ^{a−2j}⟩, of type 1 when a − 2j > 0, giving (a + 1)/2.
acceptance: ⟨ϖ³⟩: D = 1 − X + X² − X³, ∂Den = 2.
For val(L) even ∂Den is not defined by this node (D_L(1) need not vanish).

nodes.title: Special values of the hermitian Siegel series
nodes.statement: For an integral nondegenerate hermitian lattice L over an unramified F/F_0 and k ≥ 0: D_L((−q)^{−k}) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨, t(L′) ≤ k} q^{−2ℓ(L′/L)k}m(t(L′);(−q)^{−k}). hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).

nodes.title: Induction formula for the hermitian Siegel series (Terstiege)
nodes.statement: Let L^♭ be an integral hermitian lattice of rank n − 1 with fundamental invariants (a_1,…,a_{n−1}), x ⊥ L^♭ with val(x) > a_{n−1}, L = L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ and L′ = L^♭ + ⟨ϖ^{−1}x⟩, over an unramified F/F_0. Then D_L(X) = X²D_{L′}(X) + (1 − X)D_{L^♭}(−qX).
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).
Hermitian lattices are integral hermitian O_F-lattices of the parent node GN.2 integral-hermitian-lattice; ⟨1⟩^k is the self-dual lattice of rank k.

nodes.title: Densities against almost self-dual lattices
nodes.statement: Let Λ = ⟨1⟩^{n−1} ⊕ ⟨ϖ⟩ over an unramified F/F_0, L a hermitian lattice of rank n, ℓ = ⟨u_0⟩ with (u_0,u_0) = ϖ and L^♯ = L ⊕ ℓ. Then for k ≥ 0: (cancellation) Den(⟨1⟩^{n−1+k} ⊕ ⟨ϖ⟩, L) = Den(⟨1⟩^{n+1+k}, L^♯)/Den(⟨1⟩^{n+1+k}, ℓ); and Den(Λ ⊕ ⟨1⟩^k, L)/Den(⟨1⟩^{n−1+k},⟨1⟩^{n−1}) = D_{L^♯}((−q)^{−k}). Thus the Siegel series relative to Λ, Den_Λ(X,L) = D_{L^♯}(X), is a polynomial in Z[X]; if val(L) is even then Den_Λ(1,L) = 0 and ∂Den_Λ(L) = −(d/dX)Den_Λ(X,L)|_{X=1}.
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).

nodes.title: Lattices with prescribed intersection and invariant drop
nodes.statement: Let V be a nondegenerate hermitian space of dimension n over an unramified F/F_0 and L^♭ ⊂ V an O_F-lattice of rank n − 1. (1) For a lattice L′^♭ ⊂ L^♭_F, u ↦ L′^♭ + ⟨u⟩ is a bijection from [(V/L′^♭) ∖ (L′^♭_F/L′^♭)]/O_F^× onto the rank-n lattices L′ with L′ ∩ L^♭_F = L′^♭. (2) For V = L^♭_F ⊕ ⟨x⟩_F and a lattice L′, the projections give isomorphisms of cyclic O_F-modules π^♭(L′)/L′^♭ ≅ L′/(L′^♭ ⊕ L′_x) ≅ π_x(L′)/L′_x, and if x ⊥ L^♭ then vol(L′) = vol(L′^♭)vol(π_⊥(L′)). nodes.title: Hermitian densities and the Cho–Yamauchi formula in the split case
nodes.statement: Let F′/F be an unramified quadratic extension or the split algebra F × F, η the associated quadratic character (η(ϖ) = −1 inert, +1 split), and for a split hermitian lattice take L = (L_1, L_2) with the induced perfect pairing. With ℓ′ and t′ the O_{F′}-length and type (ℓ = 2ℓ′, t = 2t′ in the inert case) and m(a;T) = ∏_{i=0}^{a−1}(1 − (η(ϖ)q)^iT): (1) Den(⟨1⟩_{n+j},⟨1⟩_n) = ∏_{i=1}^n(1 − (η(ϖ)q)^{−i}T) at T = (η(ϖ)q)^{−j}; (2) there is a unique Den(T,L) ∈ Z[T] with Den((η(ϖ)q)^{−j},L) = Den(⟨1⟩_{n+j},L)/Den(⟨1⟩_{n+j},⟨1⟩_n) for j ≥ 0; (3) Den(T,L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} T^{2ℓ′(L′/L)}m(t′(L′);T), so Den(T,L) depends only on the torsion hermitian module L^∨/L; (4) Den(T,L) = (η(ϖ)T)^{ℓ′(L^∨/L)}Den(1/T,L) and deg Den(T,L) = ℓ′(L^∨/L).

nodes.title: Hermitian Siegel integrals and spherical functions (Hironaka)
nodes.statement: For a nonsingular hermitian T ∈ Herm_n(F) over an unramified F/F_0, the hermitian Siegel integral is b_T(t) = ∫_{Herm_n(F)} ν(R)^{−t}ψ(tr(TR))dR, where ψ is an additive character of F_0 of conductor O_{F_0}, dR gives Herm_n(O_F) volume 1 and ν(R) = q^{Σ e_j} for the negative elementary divisors ϖ^{−e_j} of R; it converges for Re t > 2n and continues to a rational function of q^{−t}. Hironaka's spherical function ω_T(X;s) on X_T = {X ∈ M_{2n,n}(F) : XᴴH_nX = T} (H_n = [[0,I],[I,0]]) is the K-average of ∏_i|f_i(kX)|^{s_i+ε_i} with the relative invariants f_i, with the shifts ε_i of Hironaka §1; it is K-invariant, right U(T)-invariant and rational in q^{s_i}.

Define ω_T(X;s) as a K-average over the nonvanishing locus, absolutely convergent in the stated domain, and prove the invariances.
Relate b_T to ω_T by Fourier inversion on Herm_n(F) (Hironaka Lemma 5.1, Theorem 5.2, Proposition 5.3).

nodes.title: Hironaka's functional equation and the density transform
nodes.statement: With a = val(det T), f_n(Y) = ∏_{i=0}^{n−1}(1 − (−q)^iY) and g_T(q^{−t}) = b_T(t)/f_n(q^{−t}): (1) g_T(Y) = (−1)^{a(n−1)}q^{an}Y^a g_T(q^{−2n}Y^{−1}) (Hironaka Theorem 5.6); (2) for the hermitian lattice L with Gram matrix T, D_L(X) = g_T((−q)^{−n}X). Together these give the parent node's functional equation D_L(X) = (−X)^{val L}D_L(1/X).
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).

proofSteps: (1): the spherical functions satisfy ω_T(X;z) = Γ_σ(z)ω_T(X;σz) for the Weyl group W = S_n ⋉ {±1}^n, proved for simple reflections from rank-one hermitian integrals and extended by the cocycle relation; the long element gives t ↦ 2n − t for b_T.

(2): finite Fourier orthogonality on Herm_n(O_F/ϖ^N) writes the representation count of T by I_{n+k} as an integral over R of a product of one-row Gaussian integrals ∫_{O_F}ψ(uϖ^{−e}N(x))dx = (−q)^{−e} (hermitian-finite-fourier-count); stabilization (hermitian-count-stabilizes) gives g_T((−q)^{−(n+k)}) as the density ratio, and polynomial interpolation at infinitely many points gives the identity.

n = 1, a = 2: g_T(Y) = 1 + qY + q²Y², D_L(X) = 1 − X + X², and the functional equation has sign +.

nodes.statement: Over an unramified F/F_0 with additive character ψ of conductor O_{F_0}: (1) for a unit u ∈ O_{F_0}^× and e ≥ 0, ∫_{O_F}ψ(uϖ^{−e}N_{F/F_0}(x))dx = (−q)^{−e} (Haar(O_F) = 1); (2) for m = n + k, A = I_m and T integral hermitian of rank n, the count C_N of X ∈ M_{m,n}(O_F/ϖ^N) with XᴴX ≡ T satisfies q^{−N(2mn−n²)}C_N = ∫_{ϖ^{−N}Herm_n(O_F)}ψ(−tr(TR))(∫_{M_{m,n}(O_F)}ψ(tr(RXᴴX))dX)dR, and the inner integral equals (−1)^{mΣe_j}ν(R)^{−m}.
hypotheses: F/F_0 an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic ≠ 2, q = #k_{F_0} (residue characteristic 2 allowed for the analytic statements).

(2): orthogonality of characters on the self-dual lattice Herm_n(O_F) (the trace pairing is self-dual because the different of F/F_0 is trivial); diagonalize R by integral congruence and apply (1) row by row.

nodes.title: Hermitian densities and Siegel series over a ramified extension
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a ramified quadratic extension of p-adic fields (p odd) with uniformizer u, H the hyperbolic hermitian plane with matrix [[0,u^{−1}],[−u^{−1},0]] and H_s = H^{⊕s} (self-dual of rank 2s). For hermitian O_E-lattices M, L, Den(M,L) = lim_N #Herm_{L,M}(O_E/u^{2N})/q^{N·d_{L,M}} with d_{L,M} the generic dimension. Then (Cho–Yamauchi, ramified) Den(H_s,L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨}|L′/L|^{m−2s}∏_{s−(m+t(L′))/2 < i ≤ s}(1 − q^{−2i}) for L of rank m ≤ s. For an O_E-lattice 𝐋 of the nonsplit hermitian space 𝐕 of dimension n = 2r, the normalized Siegel series Den(X,𝐋) ∈ Z[X] is defined by Den(q^{−s},𝐋) = Den(H_{r+s},𝐋)/∏_{i=s+1}^{r+s}(1 − q^{−2i}) for s ≥ 0; it satisfies Den(X,𝐋) = Σ_{𝐋⊆L⊆L^∨}X^{2 length(L/𝐋)}∏_{i=0}^{t(L)/2−1}(1 − q^{2i}X²), Den(1,𝐋) = 0, and ∂Den(𝐋) = −(d/dX)Den(X,𝐋)|_{X=1} = 2Σ_{𝐋⊆L⊆L^∨}∏_{i=1}^{t(L)/2−1}(1 − q^{2i}).

The overlattice sum is typeset with L′ ⊆ L′vee in the source (paper erratum E3); it runs over integral lattices L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨.
proofSteps: The residue space of L′ is symplectic (the hermitian form reduces to an alternating form over k for a ramified extension); count primitive representations by symplectic-isometry-count and use the saturation decomposition as in the unramified case.
Normalize by the self-dual value and interpolate in q^{−s} to define Den(X,𝐋); the weighted sum follows term by term.
Den(1,𝐋) = Den(H_r,𝐋) = 0 because 𝐕 is nonsplit and does not embed in H_r ⊗ E; differentiate the sum for ∂Den.
acceptance: In rank 2 with fundamental invariants (2b_1+1, 2b_2+1): ∂Den(𝐋) = 2Σ_{j=0}^{b_1}(1 + q + … + q^j + (b_2 − j)q^j).
s ≥ m is needed for the symplectic counts to be nonzero for every type.
Den(1,𝐋) = 0 for every 𝐋 in the nonsplit space.

nodes.title: Closed formula for the primitive derivative (He–Li–Shi–Yang)
nodes.statement: In the Krämer setting of ramified-primitive-density, let L ⊂ V be a lattice of rank n. (1) If L is not integral, ∂Pden(L) = 0. (2) If L is unimodular, ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) = 1 for n odd and 0 for n even. (3) If L = I_{n−t} ⊥ L_2 with L_2 of full type t > 0, then ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) = ∏_{ℓ=1}^{(t−1)/2}(1 − q^{2ℓ}) for t odd and (1 − χ(L_2)q^{t/2})∏_{ℓ=1}^{t/2−1}(1 − q^{2ℓ}) for t even. Consequently ∂Den(L) ∈ Z for every L, ∂Den(L) = 0 for non-integral L, and for L = L_1 ⊥ L_2 with L_1 unimodular of rank n_1: ∂Den(L) − ∂Den(L_2) = n(I_{n_2},L_2)(δ_odd(n) − δ_odd(n_2)).
hypotheses: E/F ramified, p odd; full type means every invariant of L_2 positive; in (3) t > 0 is required.
proofSteps: Theorem 6.1 of the source decomposes Pden(I_m,L,X) by the rank of the projection to H^k into finite-field isometry counts over the reduction (orthogonal-isometry-count, gaussian-binomial).
Differentiate at X = 1 and reduce the resulting alternating sums with the polynomials f_ϵ, g_ϵ, h_ϵ of §7 (Lemmas 7.7–7.16) to the product formulas; Propositions 7.5–7.6 are the full-type cases.
Integrality and the cancellation law follow by summing ∂Pden over overlattices (Corollaries 7.2–7.3, Lemma 7.4).
acceptance: n = 1, L unimodular: ∂Pden(L) = 1.
n = 2, L unimodular: ∂Pden(L) = 0.
t = 1: ∂Pden(L) = 1 (empty product); t = 2: ∂Pden = 1 − χ(L_2)q.

nodes.title: Lattice lemmas for ramified hermitian densities
nodes.statement: Over a ramified E/F (p odd): (1) for any basis with moment matrix T, a_1 + … + a_i − i is the minimal E-valuation of the i × i minors of T; (2) if L = L′ + ⟨x⟩ with L′ of rank m − 1 and x′ ∈ L′^∨ representing (x,−)|_{L′}, then t(L) = t(L′) + 1 if x′ ∈ uL′^∨ + L′ and t(L′) − 1 otherwise; (3) for integral L of rank 2m + 1 and type 2m + 1, |(L^∨)^int/L| = q^{2m}|(uL^∨)^int/L|; (4) special lattices: for r ≥ 2 and integral L^♭ in the nonsplit space with a_{n−2} < a_{n−1}, the number of integral lattices containing L^♭ with invariants (a_1,…,a_{n−2},a_{n−1} − 1,a_{n−1} − 1) is 0 or 2, and off the resulting set S_{L^♭} adding x lowers the valuation: L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ = L^{♭′} + ⟨x′⟩ with val(L^{♭′}) < val(L^♭). The Krämer analogue of (4) (He–Li–Shi–Yang Lemma 9.6) holds when the top invariant a′_n is even and fails when it is odd and a′_1 + … + a′_{n−1} = val(L^♭) − 1.

proofSteps: (1)–(2): Smith normal form of moment matrices over O_E.
(3): induction on val(L) starting from the q^{2m} isotropic vectors of a (2m+1)-dimensional quadratic space over k.

(4): the two special lattices are distinguished by the two isotropic lines of a residue plane; the reduction step chooses a basis realizing smaller invariants. The proof prints u^{e_i−1} for u^{a_i−1} (Li–Liu erratum E2).

nodes.title: The trace Z-lattice of a lattice over a totally real field
nodes.statement: For an integral quadratic O_K-lattice L in a totally positive (V,Q), the trace form Q_Z(x) = Tr_{K/Q}(Q(x)) makes L a positive definite integral quadratic Z-lattice of rank [K:Q]·rank_{O_K}L. Its real scalar extension L ⊗ ℝ is isometric to ⊕_{σ:K→ℝ}(V_σ, Q_σ), and the diagonal image of L is a discrete full lattice there. Multiplication by a ∈ O_K is self-adjoint for the trace metric with operator norm max_σ|σ(a)|.
hypotheses: K a totally real number field of degree d (d = 1 allowed) with ring of integers O_K.
(V,Q) a totally positive definite quadratic space of dimension m over K; lattices are integral quadratic O_K-lattices of GN.2, projective and possibly non-free.
proofSteps: L is finite projective over O_K, hence free of rank [K:Q]·rank L over Z; use a pseudo-basis (coefficient ideals kept) and the embedding lattice of each fractional ideal to prove discreteness and fullness.
Q_Z is integral since Tr(O_K) ⊆ Z and positive since every Q_σ is positive definite.
The adjointness and operator-norm statements are checked on each real place.

For K = Q(√5), L = O_K, Q(x) = x²: in the basis (1, ω), ω = (1+√5)/2, Q_Z = 2a² + 2ab + 3b², with Gram matrix of the polar form [[4,2],[2,6]] of determinant 20.

nodes.title: Finitely many bounded integral endomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let (M, Q_Z) be a positive definite integral quadratic Z-lattice of finite rank and C ≥ 0. Then the set of Z-linear endomorphisms T of M with Q_Z(Tx) ≤ C²Q_Z(x) for all x is finite. Consequently, on a fixed trace lattice there are only finitely many O_K-module structures compatible with the trace form, and the O_K-isometry class of an integral lattice over a totally real field is determined by its trace lattice together with its O_K-action.
hypotheses: Positive definiteness is essential.
proofSteps: T is determined by the images of a Z-basis, each of bounded norm, and IntegralLattices 2A gives finitely many vectors of bounded norm.
Apply to multiplication by a finite set of ring generators of O_K, bounded by trace_scalar_operator_bound.
The K-valued polar form is recovered from the Z-valued one by nondegeneracy of the trace pairing: B_Z(ax,y) = Tr(aB(x,y)) for all a determines B(x,y).

C = 0 leaves only T = 0.

nodes.title: Proper and ordinary masses over a totally real field
nodes.statement: Let L be a totally positive definite integral lattice of positive rank over a totally real K. The sum of the proper masses Σ 1/|SO(M)| over the proper classes in the genus of L is twice the ordinary mass Σ 1/|O(M)| over the ordinary classes: an ordinary class with an improper automorphism is one proper class with |SO(M)| = |O(M)|/2, and otherwise it splits into two proper classes with SO(M) = O(M).
hypotheses: K a totally real number field of degree d (d = 1 allowed) with ring of integers O_K.
(V,Q) a totally positive definite quadratic space of dimension m over K; lattices are integral quadratic O_K-lattices of GN.2, projective and possibly non-free.
Rank ≥ 1; in rank 0 both masses are 1.
proofSteps: O(Q)(K) has a reflection, so it has elements of determinant −1; partition the proper classes of each ordinary class by orbit–stabilizer for the action of O(Q)(K)/SO(Q)(K).
Each case contributes 2/|O(M)| to the proper sum.
Over Z this is IntegralLattices 7A; the argument is identical over O_K.

Rank 0: O = SO trivial, both masses 1, and the doubling fails.

The local type t_p(Q) ∈ {0, I, II+, II−, II, III+, III−} is: for m odd, I if v_p(d) is even and ω = −1; II± if v_p(d) is odd and ω = ±1; for m even, I if d is a square and ω = −1; II if d is a nonsquare, K_p(√d)/K_p unramified and ω = −1; III± if K_p(√d)/K_p is ramified and ω = ±1; and 0 in every other case.

nodes.title: Smooth integral models of maximal-lattice stabilizers
nodes.statement: Let F be a characteristic-0 nonarchimedean local field with ring of integers A, residue field k of cardinality q, (V,Q) nondegenerate of dimension m ≥ 3 and Λ ⊂ V a maximal integral lattice. There is a smooth affine group scheme 𝒢_Λ over A with generic fibre SO(V,Q) and 𝒢_Λ(A) the stabilizer of Λ in SO(V)(F). Except when the residue characteristic is 2, m is even and the discriminant extension is ramified, 𝒢_Λ is the schematic closure of SO(V) in GL(Λ); in that exceptional case its identity component is the closure in GL(A² ⊕ Λ) of the enlarged representation g ↦ [[I_2,0,0],[M_{12}N, M_{11}, M_{12}],[(M_{22} − I_2)N, M_{21}, M_{22}]] built from the polar-dual lattice Λ̃ = H_A^{r−1} ⊕ Aϖ^{−h}e_r ⊕ Aϖ^{−h′}f_r, N = diag(ϖ^{−h},ϖ^{−h′}), h + h′ the different exponent and h − h′ ∈ {0,1}. Its special fibre has a unipotent radical and a reductive quotient Ḡ_Λ whose type is given by the local type t_p(Q), with the component group retained; the congruence kernels are {g : (g − 1)Λ̃ ⊆ ϖ^aΛ} in the exceptional case and {g : (g − 1)Λ ⊆ ϖ^aΛ} otherwise.

nodes.title: Weil operators of a quadratic space (rank one)
nodes.statement: For a nondegenerate quadratic space (V,Q) of dimension m over a number field K, a nontrivial character ψ of 𝔸_K/K and the self-dual measures, the adelic Schwartz–Bruhat space 𝒮(V(𝔸_K)) carries the operators: multiplication by ψ(bQ(x)) (b ∈ 𝔸), normalized dilation φ ↦ |a|^{m/2}φ(ax) (a ∈ 𝔸^×), and Fourier transform for the polar pairing of Q. Θ-invariance: invariance under multiplication operators with b ∈ K and dilations with a ∈ K^× is direct; invariance under Fourier transform is Poisson summation.

nodes.title: Siegel–Weil formula for quadratic spaces of dimension > 4
nodes.statement: For a nondegenerate quadratic space (V,Q) of dimension m > 4 over a number field K and φ ∈ 𝒮(V(𝔸)), the theta integral ∫_{SO(Q)(K)\SO(Q)(𝔸)} Θ(g·φ) dg, with the invariant probability measure, equals the Eisenstein distribution E(φ) = φ(0) + Σ_{t∈K}F_φ(t) evaluated through the rational Weil operators, both sides being absolutely convergent and continuous in φ.
hypotheses: m > 4 (absolute convergence; the parabolic exponent m/4 > 1).
proofSteps: Absolute convergence of the theta integral by reduction theory (AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3) and of the Eisenstein series by the lattice height count.

Both sides are SL_2(K)-invariant distributions with the same constant term; the difference is a scalar multiple of the canonical fibre measure on each fibre, by orthogonal transitivity at a good place.
Dilation towards 0 shows the scalar vanishes (exponent −m/2 + 2 < 0 against boundedness on the reduced domain).

nodes.title: Genus double cosets and the mass of a hermitian genus
nodes.statement: Let L/K be a CM extension with K totally real and (W, h) a totally positive definite hermitian space over L. For a projective hermitian O_L-lattice M in W with integral stabilizer Stab(M) ⊂ U(𝔸_{K,f}), the isometry classes of lattices in the genus of M are in bijection with U(K)\U(𝔸_{K,f})/Stab(M); the class set is finite and each automorphism group is finite. The mass of the genus is mass(C) = Σ_{[M′] ∈ C}1/|Aut(M′)|, a positive rational number.
hypotheses: Lattices are projective, not necessarily free; the bijection is with all projective lattices of the genus, not with free Gram matrices unless the Steinitz obstruction vanishes.
proofSteps: The adelic stabilizer action on the genus is transitive by definition of the genus (local isometries); rational orbits are global isometry classes.

Finiteness of the class set and of Aut(M′): restrict scalars to a positive definite Z-lattice (number-ring-trace-lattice applied to the trace of the hermitian form) and use IntegralLattices 2C, 2G, or AA.3.4 class number finiteness.
Define the mass as a finite sum.
acceptance: One class with two automorphisms gives mass 1/2.
For L = Q(i), W = L with h = x x̄ and M = O_L: Aut(M) = μ_4, mass 1/4.
The mass counts nonfree projective lattices as well.

nodes.title: Minkowski's bound for finite subgroups of GL_N(Z)
nodes.statement: The largest order of a finite subgroup of GL_N(Z) is exp(N log N + O(N)) as N → ∞. Consequently, for a definite hermitian or quadratic lattice M of Z-rank N, log|Aut(M)| ≤ N log N + O(N).
proofSteps: Upper bound: a finite subgroup injects into GL_N(F_p) for odd p (Minkowski's lemma); combining primes in suitable residue classes bounds the p-adic valuation of the order, and summing with Σ_{p≤N}log p/p = log N + O(1) gives N log N + O(N).
Lower bound: the signed permutation matrices have order 2^N N!.
acceptance: N = 1: the maximal finite subgroup is {±1}, of order 2.
N = 2: the maximal order is 12 (the hexagonal lattice).
Signed permutations give 2^N N!, which is exp(N log N + O(N)).

nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, L a CM field generated by a p-Weil number with totally real subfield K, n ≥ 1, and C_σ a genus of unimodular hermitian O_L-lattices of rank n. Then log mass(C_σ) = (1/2)[K:Q]n² log n + O_p([K:Q]²n²), and log|C_σ| satisfies the same estimate. nodes.title: Local orbit counts of lattices stable under a semisimple endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime, O = Z_ℓ, γ an integral semisimple endomorphism of K^N (K = Q_ℓ) with characteristic polynomial ∏_i f_i^{n_i} (distinct monic irreducible f_i), δ_i = v_ℓ(disc f_i), ρ_ij = v_ℓ(Res(f_i,f_j)) and Δ = Σ_i n_i²δ_i + 2Σ_{i<j}n_in_jρ_ij. (1) The number of F^×-orbits of full R-lattices in F = K[X]/f is at most ℓ^{2δ}, for R = O[X]/f with δ = v_ℓ disc f. (2) The number of GL_n(F)-orbits of full R-lattices in F^n is at most ℓ^{(n(n−1)/2+2n)δ}. (3) The number of orbits under the centralizer of γ of full γ-stable lattices is at most ℓ^{Σ_i[n_i(n_i−1)/2+2n_i]δ_i + Σ_{i<j}n_in_jρ_ij} ≤ ℓ^{2Δ}. (4) For a monic integral polynomial of degree m with complex roots of absolute value √p and semisimple local realizations, the product over ℓ of these local orbit counts is at most D_*² ≤ (2√p)^{2m(m−1)}, with D_* the product of differences of ordered unequal root occurrences. (5) For every full γ-stable lattice M there is a conjugate H_M of ∏_iGL_{n_i}(O_{F_i}) containing Stab(M) with [H_M : Stab(M)] ≤ ℓ^{Σn_i²δ_i + Σ_{i<j}n_in_jρ_ij}.

proofSteps: (1) Normalize SM = S for the maximal order S, divide by an S-unit to get R ⊆ M ⊆ S, and dualize to ideals of colength ≤ δ (punctual-hilbert-count).
(2) Induct with a coordinate flag, normalizing prefix and quotient by block-diagonal centralizers and shears; count parabolic orbits.
(3) The disjoint-spectrum Sylvester operator X ↦ γ_2X − Xγ_1 is invertible with determinant valuation n_in_jρ_ij (Yun Lemma 4.9), which bounds the extension fibres.
(4) D_* is a nonzero rational integer whose ℓ-valuation is Δ_ℓ; almost all local factors are 1.
(5) Build H_M from the saturations of the successive quotients pr_i(M ∩ V_{≤i}) (not from M ∩ V_i).

N = 1, γ = a scalar: one orbit.
